name: Ruy Lopez: Morphy Defence
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 d6 c3 O-O h3
ideas: Pressure e5 by attacking its defender on c6
Castle early and support the d4 break with c3
h3 stops ...Bg4 pinning the f3 knight

name: Italian Game: Giuoco Pianissimo
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d3 d6 O-O O-O a4 a6 Re1
ideas: The c4 bishop eyes f7, the weakest square in Black's camp
Slow d3/c3 setup keeps the centre solid before d4
a4 gains queenside space and gives the bishop a retreat on a2

name: Two Knights: avoid the Fried Liver trap (Black)
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Na5 Bb5+ c6 dxc6 bxc6 Be2 h6 Nf3 e4 Ne5 Bd6
ideas: After Ng5, ...d5 blocks the bishop's diagonal
...Na5 chases the bishop instead of recapturing on d5
Black gives a pawn for fast development and the initiative

name: Scotch Game
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nxc6 bxc6 e5 Qe7 Qe2 Nd5 c4
ideas: Open the centre immediately with d4
Nxc6 then e5 gains space and chases the f6 knight
c4 kicks the d5 knight and grabs more space

name: Sicilian Najdorf
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be3 e5 Nb3 Be6 f3 Be7 Qd2 O-O O-O-O Nbd7
ideas: ...a6 controls b5 and prepares ...e5 or ...b5
...e5 claims the centre, accepting a backward d-pawn
Against the English Attack, race on the queenside with ...b5

name: Open Sicilian (White)
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be3 e5 Nb3 Be6 f3
ideas: Trade the c-pawn for d-pawn to open lines and lead in development
Be3, f3, Qd2 and O-O-O is the English Attack setup
Then push g4-g5 to attack the black king

name: Sicilian Alapin (White)
moves: e4 c5 c3 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 cxd4 Nf3 Nc6 cxd4 d6 Bc4
ideas: c3 prepares d4 to build a full pawn centre
Simple development, avoids the heavy Open Sicilian theory
Bc4 hits the d5 knight

name: French Defence: Advance
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 a3 c4 Nbd2 Na5
ideas: Strike the pawn chain at its base with ...c5
...Qb6 and ...Nc6 pile up on d4
...c4 then ...Na5 grabs queenside space and the b3 square

name: French Defence: Winawer
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3+ bxc3 Ne7 Qg4 O-O
ideas: Pin the c3 knight to increase pressure on e4
Give up the bishop to damage White's pawn structure
Black targets the doubled c-pawns later

name: Caro-Kann: Classical
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6 Nf3 Nd7 h5 Bh7 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3 e6
ideas: ...c6 supports ...d5 without blocking the light-squared bishop
Develop the bishop outside the pawn chain to f5
Solid structure; aim for a good endgame

name: Caro-Kann: Advance
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6 Be2 c5 Be3 Nd7 O-O Ne7
ideas: Get the bishop out to f5 before ...e6
Hit the centre with ...c5
The e7 knight heads to c6 or f5

name: Scandinavian Defence
moves: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5 d4 Nf6 Nf3 c6 Bc4 Bf5 Bd2 e6
ideas: Challenge e4 immediately
The queen on a5 pins along the diagonal and stays safe
Easy development: ...Nf6, ...c6, ...Bf5, ...e6

name: Pirc Defence
moves: e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 Bg7 Qd2 c6 f3 b5
ideas: Let White build a centre, then attack it
The fianchettoed bishop pressures d4 and the long diagonal
...c6 and ...b5 start queenside play

name: Queen's Gambit Declined
moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Be7 Bf4 O-O e3 c5 dxc5 Bxc5
ideas: Hold d5 with ...e6
Develop quickly and castle
...c5 frees the position

name: Queen's Gambit (White)
moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 cxd5 exd5 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O Bd3 Nbd7 Qc2 Re8 Nge2
ideas: c4 challenges Black's d5 pawn
The Exchange variation gives a clear plan: the minority attack
Push b4-b5 to create a weakness on c6

name: Queen's Gambit Accepted
moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3 Nf6 e3 e6 Bxc4 c5 O-O a6
ideas: Take the pawn but do not try to keep it
Use the time to develop and hit d4 with ...c5
...a6 and ...b5 gain queenside space

name: Slav Defence
moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3 e6 Bxc4 Bb4
ideas: ...c6 protects d5 while keeping the c8 bishop free
Take on c4 and develop the bishop to f5
...Bb4 pins and fights for e4

name: London System
moves: d4 d5 Bf4 Nf6 e3 e6 Nf3 c5 c3 Nc6 Nbd2 Bd6 Bg3 O-O Bd3
ideas: Same setup against almost anything: d4, Bf4, e3, Nf3, c3, Bd3
Keep the bishop when Black offers a trade with ...Bd6
Typical plan: Ne5 and a kingside attack

name: King's Indian Defence
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3 O-O Be2 e5 O-O Nc6 d5 Ne7
ideas: Allow a big white centre, then strike with ...e5
After d5, Black attacks on the kingside with ...f5
White attacks on the queenside: a race

name: Nimzo-Indian Defence
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Qc2 O-O a3 Bxc3+ Qxc3 d5 Nf3 dxc4 Qxc4 b6
ideas: Pin the c3 knight to fight for e4
Trade bishop for knight when it damages White or wins time
...b6 and ...Ba6 or ...Bb7 develop the last piece

name: Grünfeld Defence
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5 e4 Nxc3 bxc3 Bg7 Nf3 c5 Be3 Qa5
ideas: Let White build a big centre
Attack it with the g7 bishop, ...c5 and ...Nc6
Black often gets queenside pressure along the c-file

name: Dutch Defence: Stonewall
moves: d4 f5 g3 Nf6 Bg2 e6 Nf3 d5 O-O Bd6 c4 c6
ideas: ...f5 controls e4
The pawn wall c6-d5-e6-f5 gives a stable centre
Plan: ...Ne4, ...Qf6 and a kingside attack

name: English Opening
moves: c4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 g3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5 Bg2 Nb6 Nf3 Nc6 O-O Be7
ideas: A reversed Sicilian with an extra tempo
The g2 bishop pressures the long diagonal
Play for d3/a3/b4 and queenside expansion

name: Vienna Game
moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nc6 d3 Bb4 Bg5 h6 Bxf6 Bxc3+ bxc3 Qxf6
ideas: Nc3 supports a later f4 break
Bc4 eyes f7
Simple development with a flexible centre

name: King's Gambit Accepted
moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 d5 exd5 Nf6 Bb5+ c6 dxc6 bxc6 Bc4
ideas: Sacrifice the f-pawn for open lines and the centre
Nf3 stops ...Qh4+
Recapture f4 later and attack along the f-file

name: Petrov Defence
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4 d4 d5 Bd3 Nc6 O-O Be7
ideas: Counter-attack e4 instead of defending e5
Never take on e4 before ...d6 kicks the e5 knight
Very solid and symmetrical

name: Philidor: Legal's mate pattern
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d6 Bc4 Bg4 Nc3 g6 Nxe5 Bxd1 Bxf7+ Ke7 Nd5#
ideas: A pinned knight is not always really pinned
Bxf7+ and Nd5# are the mating pattern
Learn to spot when the opponent's pin is fake

name: Alekhine's Defence
moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 Nf3 Bg4 Be2 e6 O-O Be7 h3 Bh5
ideas: Lure White's pawns forward
Then attack the overextended centre
...Bg4 pressures d4 by pinning the f3 knight
